parts.visual:
The PM wants the 'Buy Now' button to be Green. The CEO wants the button to be Red. They argue in a meeting for 2 hours. A professional PM stops the meeting and says: 'Let's just ask the algorithm.' They launch both buttons. 50% of users see Green, 50% see Red. Three days later, the data shows Red generated 20% more revenue. End of argument.

The Experiment:
1. A/B Testing: The process of serving two different versions of a feature to two random groups of users at the exact same time, to mathematically prove which one performs better.
2. The End of Opinions: In a high-functioning product team, the Highest Paid Person's Opinion (HiPPO) is irrelevant. Only the results of the A/B test matter.
parts.audio: If you have an opinion, we will listen. If you have data, you win. A/B testing shifts product development from 'Who is the best debater in the meeting?' to 'Who actually knows what the user wants?'

questions.question: What is the 'Control' group in an A/B Test?
options: The users who control the app.

Group A. They see the original, unchanged version of the app. They act as the baseline. Group B sees the new 'Variant'. If you don't have a Control group, you cannot mathematically prove that your change actually caused the increase in clicks.
questions.correct_answer: Group A. They see the original, unchanged version of the app. They act as the baseline. Group B sees the new 'Variant'. If you don't have a Control group, you cannot mathematically prove that your change actually caused the increase in clicks.
questions.explanation: You cannot measure progress without a baseline.

questions.question: Listen to the data scientist rejecting an A/B test result. Why is the test invalid?
questions.tts_text: We ran the test for 4 hours. 10 people saw the Red button and 12 people saw the Green button. The Green button got one more click! The PM wants to launch Green to millions of users. I told them no. It is not statistically significant.
options: Because green is an ugly color.

Statistical Significance. You cannot make massive business decisions based on 22 people clicking a button. The result might just be random luck. You must run the test until thousands of users participate to prove the result is a mathematical certainty, not a fluke.
Because the data scientist hates the PM.
questions.correct_answer: Statistical Significance. You cannot make massive business decisions based on 22 people clicking a button. The result might just be random luck. You must run the test until thousands of users participate to prove the result is a mathematical certainty, not a fluke.

questions.question: What is the danger of testing too many things at the exact same time?
options: The Isolation Problem. If you change the button color, the headline text, AND the price all in the same A/B test, and sales go up 30%, you have no idea WHICH change actually caused the success. You must test one variable at a time.
questions.correct_answer: The Isolation Problem. If you change the button color, the headline text, AND the price all in the same A/B test, and sales go up 30%, you have no idea WHICH change actually caused the success. You must test one variable at a time.

questions.question: What is the 'HiPPO' effect in product meetings, which A/B testing destroys?
options: Highest Paid Person's Opinion. Without data, the CEO or senior executives automatically win every argument just because of their rank. A/B testing democratizes the process, allowing a junior designer to beat the CEO if their design gets more clicks.
questions.correct_answer: Highest Paid Person's Opinion. Without data, the CEO or senior executives automatically win every argument just because of their rank. A/B testing democratizes the process, allowing a junior designer to beat the CEO if their design gets more clicks.
